title: Retention policy JSON examples (v1) — test + customer scenarios
body:
Purpose
- Working collection of retention policy JSON snippets used by:
  - unit/integration tests (golden effective-policy results)
  - manual QA via Console + control-plane API
  - customer scenario walkthroughs (Sales/SE + Security reviews)
- Not a formal spec. Canonical behavior lives in Confluence “Retention policy schema and evaluation” + ADR.

Notes / conventions (please read before copy/paste)
- Policy documents below use a common shape but may include intentionally-invalid examples for validation tests.
- Time formats:
  - prefer days ("30d", "90d", "365d") for readability in customer docs
  - engine accepts ISO-8601 duration too (e.g., "P90D") — check parser expectations
- Data types referenced in examples (v1 scope):
  - "audit_logs" (security/compliance audit log store)
  - "admin_activity" (Console + admin actions, may overlap with audit logs depending on event type)
  - "inference_request_metadata" (request IDs, timestamps, model, token counts, status; NOT raw prompts/responses)
  - "telemetry_analytics" (eligible analytics tables only; not all raw infra logs)
  - "operational_logs" (selected application/service logs where we have explicit eligibility; many remain SRE/vendor governed)
- Precedence reminder (expected evaluation order):
  1) legal hold / exception override (highest)
  2) tenant override
  3) org/account default
  4) system defaults (lowest)
  Plus environment-specific overrides (prod vs staging) layered within a given policy.
- Region handling:
  - some tenants are single-region; others multi-region.
  - policy can set per-region retention if storage is region-partitioned.

================================================================================
Example 0 — Minimal “system default” style (used in seed data tests)
================================================================================

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "system-default",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "system"
  },
  "defaults": {
    "timezone": "UTC",
    "retention": {
      "audit_logs": "365d",
      "admin_activity": "365d",
      "inference_request_metadata": "30d",
      "telemetry_analytics": "30d"
    }
  },
  "guardrails": {
    "min_retention": {
      "audit_logs": "30d",
      "admin_activity": "30d",
      "inference_request_metadata": "7d",
      "telemetry_analytics": "7d"
    },
    "max_retention": {
      "audit_logs": "730d",
      "admin_activity": "730d",
      "inference_request_metadata": "365d",
      "telemetry_analytics": "365d"
    },
    "allow_never_delete": false
  }
}
```

Comments
- This is the “safe default” profile referenced by product docs.
- Guardrails here represent platform-level limits; tenants can be stricter (shorter) but not outside min/max.

================================================================================
Example 1 — Tenant override: enterprise asks for 90-day metadata + 365-day audit logs
================================================================================

Scenario
- Hosted tenant wants:
  - audit logs: 365 days
  - inference request metadata: 90 days
  - telemetry analytics: 90 days (eligible tables)

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tenant-10488-enterprise-90d-metadata",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_10488",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted"
  },
  "effective_from": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "365d",
    "admin_activity": "365d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "90d",
    "telemetry_analytics": "90d"
  },
  "notes": "Created for enterprise security review; aligns with SOC2 evidence expectations. No raw payload retention changes."
}
```

Test assertions (expected)
- Validation passes (within guardrails).
- Effective policy for tenant tnt_10488 (prod) reflects overrides above.

================================================================================
Example 2 — Per-environment override: staging/dev shorter than prod
================================================================================

Scenario
- Dedicated tenant wants prod audit logs kept 365d, but staging only 30d to reduce storage.

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tnt_10511-prod-vs-staging",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_10511",
    "deployment_mode": "dedicated"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "365d",
    "admin_activity": "365d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "30d",
    "telemetry_analytics": "30d"
  },
  "overrides": [
    {
      "when": {
        "environment": "staging"
      },
      "set": {
        "audit_logs": "30d",
        "admin_activity": "30d",
        "inference_request_metadata": "7d",
        "telemetry_analytics": "7d"
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "environment": "dev"
      },
      "set": {
        "audit_logs": "30d",
        "admin_activity": "30d",
        "inference_request_metadata": "7d",
        "telemetry_analytics": "7d"
      }
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Prod retains longer for auditability; non-prod minimized." 
}
```

QA checklist
- Console effective-policy view should show different “effective retention” when toggling environment.
- Enforcement workers must use effective policy (not base policy) per environment partitions.

================================================================================
Example 3 — Multi-region: EU tenant sets stricter telemetry retention in EU
================================================================================

Scenario
- Tenant is multi-region (us-east-1 + eu-west-1)
- They want:
  - audit logs: 365d everywhere
  - telemetry: 90d in US but 30d in EU (privacy posture)

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tnt_multi_region_eu_stricter_telemetry",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_20031",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "365d",
    "admin_activity": "365d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "30d",
    "telemetry_analytics": "90d"
  },
  "overrides": [
    {
      "when": {
        "region": "eu-west-1"
      },
      "set": {
        "telemetry_analytics": "30d"
      }
    }
  ],
  "notes": "EU telemetry shortened. Ensure partition TTL is region-specific (eligible tables)."
}
```

Implementation gotchas
- If telemetry tables aren’t region-partitioned, this policy should either (a) be rejected as unenforceable, or (b) surface as ‘configured but not enforceable’ (TBD product behavior). Do NOT silently ignore.

================================================================================
Example 4 — Private deployment: customer-managed storage + Redwood control-plane policy
================================================================================

Scenario
- Redwood Private (VPC) deployment where customer controls certain backends.
- Policy still stored in control plane; enforcement may be:
  - “enforced_by_redwood” for audit log service
  - “customer_managed” for some operational logs

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "private-vpc-hybrid-enforcement",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_private_778",
    "deployment_mode": "private"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "365d",
    "admin_activity": "365d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "14d",
    "telemetry_analytics": "30d",
    "operational_logs": "30d"
  },
  "enforcement": {
    "audit_logs": "enforced_by_redwood",
    "admin_activity": "enforced_by_redwood",
    "inference_request_metadata": "enforced_by_redwood",
    "telemetry_analytics": "enforced_by_redwood",
    "operational_logs": "customer_managed"
  },
  "notes": "Operational logs governed by customer logging stack; Console should disclose which are customer-managed."
}
```

TODO
- Confirm final schema for `enforcement` (string enum vs structured object). Keep this example in sync with Console copy.

================================================================================
Example 5 — Legal hold: freeze deletions for audit logs + admin activity
================================================================================

Scenario
- Tenant has legal hold due to investigation.
- Hold should prevent deletion regardless of configured retention.
- Hold can be scoped (data types + optional timeframe).

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tnt_10488-legal-hold-2025q1",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_10488"
  },
  "legal_holds": [
    {
      "hold_id": "lh_2025_02_07_incident_review",
      "status": "active",
      "created_at": "2025-02-07T19:12:00Z",
      "created_by": "security-eng",
      "reason": "Customer-requested legal hold during investigation; preserve audit/admin logs.",
      "applies_to": {
        "data_types": ["audit_logs", "admin_activity"],
        "region": "*",
        "environment": "prod"
      }
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Hold should override retention enforcement. Exports allowed; deletions blocked."
}
```

Expected enforcement behavior
- Retention workers should:
  - skip deletions for held data types
  - emit an audit event (or structured log) indicating hold prevented deletion
  - still enforce other data types (e.g., telemetry) unless held

================================================================================
Example 6 — Exception workflow: temporary extension beyond tenant’s normal policy
================================================================================

Scenario
- Support/GRC grants a time-bound exception: extend inference_request_metadata from 30d -> 60d for debugging.
- Must be time-bound + documented.

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tnt_30012-debug-exception-60d-metadata",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_30012",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted"
  },
  "retention": {
    "inference_request_metadata": "60d"
  },
  "exception": {
    "exception_id": "exc_2025_02_12_support_debug",
    "approved_by": "Olga Petrov",
    "requested_by": "Dev Patel",
    "expires_at": "2025-04-15T00:00:00Z",
    "ticket": "Jira:SUP-4831"
  },
  "notes": "Temporary extension for debugging; revert after expiry."
}
```

Open question
- Do we model exception as a separate record that overlays the base policy, vs embedding inside policy? (Leaning separate record; this example may be outdated.)

================================================================================
Example 7 — Intentionally INVALID: below minimum retention (should fail validation)
================================================================================

Scenario
- Tenant attempts to set audit logs to 7 days (below min 30d).

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "invalid-too-short-audit",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_bad_01"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "7d"
  },
  "notes": "Expected: validation error min_retention.audit_logs violated"
}
```

Expected error (example)
- code: RETENTION_OUT_OF_BOUNDS
- field: retention.audit_logs
- message: "audit_logs retention must be >= 30d"

================================================================================
Example 8 — Intentionally INVALID: attempt to set “never delete” (disallowed)
================================================================================

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "invalid-never-delete",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_bad_02"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "never"
  },
  "notes": "Expected: validation error allow_never_delete=false"
}
```

Comments
- Legal hold is the only sanctioned way to effectively “never delete” for a time period.
- If customer requires indefinite retention, that needs explicit product/legal review (and likely separate storage/export path).

================================================================================
Example 9 — “Disable telemetry analytics storage” (strict posture) — if supported
================================================================================

Scenario
- Customer requests no analytics storage beyond minimal operational needs.
- We currently expect some telemetry to remain for reliability (SRE constraints). If we support tenant-configurable telemetry retention = 7d (min), show that.

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "tnt_strict_minimum_telemetry",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_strict_900",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted"
  },
  "retention": {
    "telemetry_analytics": "7d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "7d"
  },
  "notes": "Customer asked to minimize stored metadata/analytics. Ensure dashboards still function w/ reduced lookback."
}
```

SRE note
- Any enforcement that reduces retention must ensure alerting/lookback windows are compatible.

================================================================================
Example 10 — Org-level default + tenant overrides (used in precedence golden tests)
================================================================================

Org policy (account default)

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "org_acme_defaults",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "org",
    "org_id": "org_acme"
  },
  "retention": {
    "audit_logs": "365d",
    "admin_activity": "365d",
    "inference_request_metadata": "30d",
    "telemetry_analytics": "30d"
  },
  "notes": "Org-wide defaults for ACME family of tenants"
}
```

Tenant override within org

```json
{
  "version": "2025-01-01",
  "policy_name": "org_acme_tenant_special_case",
  "scope": {
    "scope_type": "tenant",
    "org_id": "org_acme",
    "tenant_id": "tnt_acme_subsidiary_3"
  },
  "retention": {
    "inference_request_metadata": "90d"
  },
  "notes": "Subsidiary 3 requires longer metadata retention for internal investigations"
}
```

Golden test expectation
- Effective:
  - audit_logs/admin_activity: 365d (from org)
  - inference_request_metadata: 90d (tenant override)
  - telemetry_analytics: 30d (from org)

================================================================================
Example 11 — Backward compatibility: legacy fields (migration tests)
================================================================================

Scenario
- Older tenants might have legacy config keys. This example is for migration/compat tests only.

```json
{
  "legacy_version": "2024-09",
  "tenant_id": "tnt_legacy_55",
  "log_retention_days": 365,
  "metadata_retention_days": 30,
  "notes": "Migration should map log_retention_days -> audit_logs/admin_activity, metadata_retention_days -> inference_request_metadata"
}
```

Expected migration output (conceptual)
- New policy record created with version 2025-01-01 and the mapped retention values.

================================================================================
Example 12 — Audit log export boundary behavior (for exporter tests)
================================================================================

Scenario
- Export request for audit logs should not include events older than retention cutoff.
- Export response should include metadata warning if customer requested a window older than retention.

Inputs used by exporter integration tests

```json
{
  "export_request": {
    "tenant_id": "tnt_10488",
    "data_type": "audit_logs",
    "format": "jsonl",
    "from": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "to": "2025-02-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "assumed_effective_retention": "365d",
  "expected": {
    "effective_from": "2024-02-02T00:00:00Z",
    "include_warning": true
  }
}
```

Notes
- Keep consistent with audit-log-exporter behavior (see exporter PR). Not sure final field names.

================================================================================
Scratch / TODOs
================================================================================
- Confirm exact schema keys:
  - do we keep `defaults` vs top-level `retention` consistently?
  - do we use `overrides[]` with `when/set`, or `rules[]` with `match/apply`? (Spec may prefer one.)
- Need one example covering “effective policy display” fields (e.g., computed next run time / last run).
- Add example for “data residency + retention combined” (if policy ties to region pinning).

Contacts
